name: Claude Fable 5
note: New flagship for difficult research, engineering, scientific, and security work; benchmark figures are vendor-reported unless noted.
coding_basis: Terminal-Bench 2.1, FrontierSWE, SWE Marathon, and PostTrainBench results in the Fable 5 system card; scaled against the same July 2026 frontier set.
writing_basis: Long-form professional-task quality in GDPval-AA and AA-Briefcase plus Anthropic human-preference evaluations; few writing-only public benchmarks exist.
chat_basis: Arena-style human preference, instruction-following, and long-context dialogue evidence; normalized below the strongest style-specialized result.
science_basis: GPQA Diamond, Humanity's Last Exam, and Anthropic science/research evaluations; current best-in-class anchor on this 0-100 scale.
computerUse_basis: OSWorld, BrowseComp, MCP Atlas, AutomationBench, OfficeQA Pro, and SpreadsheetBench 2 agentic results.
cybersecurity_basis: KCB 2.0 and Anthropic cyber/CTF system-card evaluations; current high-end anchor, with safeguards considered separately from capability.

name: Claude Opus 4.8
note: General-purpose Opus flagship immediately below Fable 5; standard API pricing shown.
coding_basis: Strong Terminal-Bench 2.1, FrontierSWE, SWE Marathon, and PostTrainBench placement in Anthropic and independent agentic evaluations.
writing_basis: Top-tier GDPval-AA and AA-Briefcase professional deliverables plus strong human preference for editing, voice, and long-form synthesis.
chat_basis: High Arena-style human preference and instruction-following quality; especially strong conversational tone and nuanced assistance.
science_basis: GPQA Diamond, Humanity's Last Exam, and research-agent results; slightly below Fable 5 and the best high-compute science models.
computerUse_basis: OSWorld, BrowseComp, MCP Atlas, AutomationBench, OfficeQA Pro, and SpreadsheetBench 2 indicate elite general agent performance.
cybersecurity_basis: Anthropic cyber system-card and KCB 2.0 evidence show very high exploit and security-reasoning capability, just below Fable 5.

name: Claude Sonnet 5
note: Standard list price is shown; Anthropic has temporary launch pricing of $2 input and $10 output through 2026-08-31.
coding_basis: Anthropic cost-performance curves and partner evaluations show Opus-class sustained coding, tool use, debugging, and brownfield issue resolution.
writing_basis: Professional-task and human-preference evidence; close to Opus quality but optimized more heavily for execution speed and cost.
chat_basis: Human-preference and instruction-following evidence plus efficient conversational behavior; normalized near the top of the field.
science_basis: GPQA/HLE-family reasoning and general knowledge evidence; strong frontier result but below the highest-compute science flagships.
computerUse_basis: OSWorld and BrowseComp cost-performance curves plus multi-step tool-use partner evaluations indicate near-Opus execution quality.
cybersecurity_basis: Anthropic reports materially lower cyber capability than its Opus models; scaled conservatively from system-card cyber evaluations.

name: Claude Haiku 4.5
note: Anthropic's fastest current small model; smaller context and lower reasoning ceiling than the 2026 Claude flagships.
coding_basis: SWE-bench Verified and agentic coding evidence from Anthropic's Haiku 4.5 system card; normalized well below 2026 frontier flagships.
writing_basis: Human-preference and instruction-following evidence supports polished short-form output, with less depth on long professional deliverables.
chat_basis: Fast conversational instruction following and Anthropic human-preference evaluations; latency helps interaction but not raw capability score.
science_basis: GPQA Diamond and general reasoning evaluations in the system card; capable but meaningfully behind newer high-compute models.
computerUse_basis: Computer-use and tool-use evaluations show useful low-latency agency, limited by smaller reasoning and context budgets.
cybersecurity_basis: System-card cyber evaluations and model scale imply a much lower advanced CTF/exploit ceiling than Opus/Fable models.

name: GPT-5.6 Sol
note: Current highest-capability GPT-5.6 tier and OpenAI's flagship for professional work; standard API pricing shown.
coding_basis: State-of-the-art vendor-reported Terminal-Bench 2.1 plus strong SWE Marathon, FrontierSWE, and professional coding-agent results.
writing_basis: GDPval-AA, AA-Briefcase, and professional deliverable evaluations; excellent precision, though Claude Opus remains the style anchor.
chat_basis: Human preference, instruction following, and professional assistant evaluations; strong but optimized more for work than casual style.
science_basis: GeneBench Pro, GPQA Diamond, Humanity's Last Exam, and expert science tasks place Sol at the current frontier anchor.
computerUse_basis: BrowseComp, OfficeQA Pro, SpreadsheetBench 2, MCP Atlas, AutomationBench, and first-party computer/tool-use evaluations.
cybersecurity_basis: ExploitBench, ExploitGym, KCB 2.0, and professional cyber evaluations support a current best-in-class estimate.

name: GPT-5.6 Terra
note: Balanced GPT-5.6 tier for everyday professional and agentic workloads.
coding_basis: GPT-5.6 family Terminal-Bench and software-agent evidence, discounted from Sol for its lower-compute tier.
writing_basis: Professional deliverable, instruction-following, and human-preference evidence; strong balance of quality and response cost.
chat_basis: OpenAI human-preference and instruction-following evaluations; balanced tier is especially suitable for general assistants.
science_basis: GPT-5.6 family GPQA/HLE/GeneBench evidence, conservatively normalized below Sol's maximum-reasoning results.
computerUse_basis: GPT-5.6 family BrowseComp and office/tool-use evaluations, adjusted for the balanced compute tier.
cybersecurity_basis: GPT-5.6 family ExploitBench/ExploitGym evidence, scaled below Sol because tier-specific public results are limited.

name: GPT-5.6 Luna
note: Fastest and lowest-cost GPT-5.6 tier; tier-specific public benchmark disclosure is limited, so estimates are conservative.
coding_basis: GPT-5.6 family software-engineering evidence adjusted downward for the low-cost, low-latency compute tier.
writing_basis: OpenAI instruction-following and professional-task evidence; fewer tier-specific writing results are public.
chat_basis: Human-preference and instruction-following evidence plus fast interactive latency; raw quality remains below Terra and Sol.
science_basis: GPT-5.6 family GPQA/HLE evidence, scaled conservatively because Luna-specific maximum-reasoning results are not published.
computerUse_basis: GPT-5.6 family tool-use and computer-task results adjusted for the faster, cheaper inference tier.
cybersecurity_basis: Family ExploitBench/ExploitGym evidence with a conservative tier discount; no comprehensive Luna-only cyber table is public.

name: GPT-5.5 Pro
note: Highest-compute GPT-5.5 reasoning tier, retained as the fourth current flagship option alongside the newer GPT-5.6 family; it does not expose native computer use.
coding_basis: FrontierSWE, PostTrainBench, Terminal-Bench, and long-horizon coding-agent evaluations; still elite but superseded by GPT-5.6 Sol.
writing_basis: GDPval-AA, AA-Briefcase, and professional deliverable evidence; high quality but expensive and slower than newer tiers.
chat_basis: Instruction-following and human-preference evidence, with latency and over-deliberation reducing suitability for ordinary chat.
science_basis: GPQA Diamond, Humanity's Last Exam, and high-compute expert reasoning results; near the frontier science anchor.
computerUse_basis: Strong browser/agent reasoning on BrowseComp-style tasks, but the official model lacks native computer-use support.
cybersecurity_basis: KCB 2.0 and high-compute security-reasoning evidence; below the newer Sol/Opus/Fable frontier.

name: Grok 4.5
note: New xAI flagship; official benchmark numbers are vendor-reported and reflect selected agent harnesses.
coding_basis: DeepSWE 1.0 62%, DeepSWE 1.1 53%, SWE Marathon 29%, Terminal-Bench 2.1 83.3%, and SWE-Bench Pro 64.7% reported by xAI.
writing_basis: Arena-style preference and professional-generation evidence; fewer writing-only public evaluations than for Claude or GPT flagships.
chat_basis: Strong human-preference placement and conversational personality, normalized below the most consistent general-assistant leaders.
science_basis: GPQA Diamond, AIME/HMMT-family math, and frontier reasoning results reported in xAI's launch materials.
computerUse_basis: Terminal-Bench 2.1, agentic software work, tool calling, and research-agent evidence indicate high autonomous execution ability.
cybersecurity_basis: CTF/KCB-style and terminal-agent evidence supports a high estimate; comprehensive independent cyber reporting remains limited.

name: Grok 4.1 Fast Reasoning
note: Latest established fast/reasoning Grok tier alongside Grok 4.5; standard cache-miss API pricing shown.
coding_basis: BFCL v4 and xAI coding/tool-use evaluations; optimized for throughput rather than maximum software-engineering depth.
writing_basis: General human-preference and instruction-following evidence; competent but less nuanced than premium frontier models.
chat_basis: Fast interactive behavior and human-preference evidence make it a strong chat model despite a lower hard-reasoning ceiling.
science_basis: Grok Fast-family GPQA Diamond 85.7 and AIME 92 evidence, normalized against newer July 2026 models.
computerUse_basis: BFCL v4 72%, research-agent 63.9%, FRAMES 87.6%, and X Browse 56.3% reported by xAI.
cybersecurity_basis: Tool-use and terminal reasoning imply solid defensive analysis; limited model-specific Cybench/CTF disclosure lowers confidence.

name: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview
note: Latest currently available Gemini Pro tier; preview model. Price shown is the standard rate for prompts up to 200K tokens; longer prompts cost $4 input and $18 output per million.
coding_basis: SWE-bench/Terminal-Bench-family agentic coding and Google vibe-coding evaluations; strong but below the July coding leaders.
writing_basis: Professional multimodal generation, instruction following, and human-preference evidence; strong synthesis with some verbosity variance.
chat_basis: Arena-style human preference and multimodal assistant quality support a near-frontier conversational score.
science_basis: GPQA Diamond, Humanity's Last Exam, MMMU-Pro, and long-context scientific reasoning are among the model's strongest areas.
computerUse_basis: Agentic tool use, custom tools, BrowseComp-style research, and multimodal interface reasoning; no dedicated native computer-use model claim.
cybersecurity_basis: Strong general reasoning and code analysis, but limited model-specific Cybench/CTF disclosure; scored conservatively.

name: Gemini 3.6 Flash
note: Just-launched stable fast tier; Google reports improved quality and token efficiency over Gemini 3.5 Flash.
coding_basis: Google agentic coding and code-generation evaluations show near-Pro capability at Flash latency; independent post-launch data is still sparse.
writing_basis: Human-preference, instruction-following, and multimodal generation evidence; concise and efficient rather than style-leading.
chat_basis: Fast multimodal dialogue and human-preference evidence; optimized for responsive assistant workloads.
science_basis: GPQA/MMMU/HLE-family evidence reported at launch, scaled below Pro and high-compute science flagships.
computerUse_basis: Google reports improved OSWorld performance and computer-use efficiency, making agentic GUI work a standout capability.
cybersecurity_basis: Strong code and agent reasoning, but it is not the separate 3.5 Flash Cyber specialist; limited public Cybench data.
weaknesses: less deep than Pro on hard science

name: GLM-5.2
note: Latest GLM flagship. Official Z.ai API pricing is used; open weights are also available.
coding_basis: FrontierSWE trails Claude Opus 4.8 by about 1 point and exceeds GPT-5.5 by about 1; also strong Code Arena, DeepSWE, ProgramBench, and PostTrainBench results.
writing_basis: Professional deliverable and bilingual generation evidence; fewer independent English style-preference results than Western flagships.
chat_basis: General preference, instruction-following, and bilingual assistant evidence; normalized below the strongest established chat models.
science_basis: GPQA/HLE/math and general expert-reasoning results in the GLM-5.2 report; highly capable but not the science anchor.
computerUse_basis: OfficeQA Pro, SpreadsheetBench 2, MCP Atlas, AutomationBench, BrowseComp, and long-horizon coding-agent evidence.
cybersecurity_basis: KCB 2.0, coding, and terminal-agent evidence support a strong estimate; public safety/cyber detail is thinner than Anthropic or OpenAI.

name: Qwen3.7-Max
note: Latest Qwen Max flagship. Alibaba Cloud Model Studio international standard pricing is used, excluding temporary regional discounts.
coding_basis: SWE-Bench Verified 80.4 and Terminal-Bench 2.0-Terminus 69.7 reported by Together, plus Alibaba agentic coding evaluations.
writing_basis: Strong multilingual and long-form generation with good instruction following; style-preference evidence is less extensive than Arena leaders.
chat_basis: Multilingual assistant and preference evidence; strong general interaction, with verbosity noted by Artificial Analysis.
science_basis: GPQA Diamond 92.4 and HMMT February 2026 97.1 reported by Together, plus Alibaba reasoning benchmarks.
computerUse_basis: Terminal-Bench, agentic tool use, browser/research workflows, and Alibaba's agent-frontier evaluations.
cybersecurity_basis: High coding and terminal scores imply strong security reasoning; sparse model-specific Cybench/CTF reporting keeps the estimate below leaders.

name: DeepSeek-V4-Pro Preview
note: Latest DeepSeek flagship API model and hybrid thinking/non-thinking preview; official cache-miss price is used.
coding_basis: DeepSeek's V4-Pro launch coding and agent benchmarks plus public software-engineering comparisons; preview status and limited independent replication reduce confidence.
writing_basis: Strong long-context and bilingual generation, but limited current Arena writing-style evidence for the Pro preview.
chat_basis: Hybrid thinking supports flexible conversation; scored conservatively from instruction-following and general preference evidence.
science_basis: DeepSeek reasoning-family GPQA, math, and expert-domain evidence, with V4-Pro positioned as its strongest current reasoner.
computerUse_basis: Launch emphasis on stronger agent capabilities, coding, and tool use; no comprehensive independent OSWorld table was available.
cybersecurity_basis: Strong code reasoning and agent autonomy imply high CTF/security potential; limited V4-Pro-specific Cybench disclosure caps the score.

name: Kimi K3
note: API is live; full open weights were announced for 2026-07-27. Standard cache-miss input pricing is shown; cached input is $0.30 per million tokens.
coding_basis: DeepSWE v1.1 67.3 plus Kimi's Terminal-Bench 2.1, ProgramBench, SWE Marathon, FrontierSWE, PostTrainBench, MLS Bench Lite, and KCB 2.0 table.
writing_basis: OfficeQA Pro, SpreadsheetBench 2, GDPval-AA, AA-Briefcase, and Kimi's professional artifact-generation evaluations.
chat_basis: Human-preference and instruction-following evidence plus strong knowledge-work interaction; fewer mature Arena samples because it is newly launched.
science_basis: Kimi's full GPQA/HLE/math and multimodal benchmark table, including MMMU-Pro and PerceptionBench; scaled below the science leaders.
computerUse_basis: OfficeQA Pro, SpreadsheetBench 2, MCP Atlas, AutomationBench, BrowseComp 90.4 without context management, and strong agentic coding results.
cybersecurity_basis: KCB 2.0 and terminal/coding-agent evidence show high security-task competence; results are primarily vendor-run.
